fields.question: Change set 01M79KHH (Bring-your-own docs) asks for a 'Bring your own agent' page with one worked example per level. What are the levels? (Today: conductor spawns follow `rhiza guide <role>` with no per-role invoke; invokes exist on agent steps and on leaves/checks role tables; rhiza skill check checks builder, verifier and check roles.)
fields.reasoning: Conductor spawns take no invoke (run spawn starts each child with 'follow rhiza guide <role>'), so a team's own role skill is reachable today only through a leaves or checks role table, which ship-change-classic has; the conduct step's prompt is the place a team's own conductor goes. A level built on a second agent adapter would describe code that does not exist (claude-code is the only adapter), so the agent in 'bring your own agent' is the team's own agent session and skill. Example files kept valid by a test follow docs/examples/workflows and TestDocsExampleWorkflows.
fields.statement: The Bring your own agent page has three levels, each with one worked example: a skill (a team's installed skill plays one role: rhiza skill check it, then put it in a role table's invoke in a workflow forked from ship-change-classic), a conductor (the team's own conduct skill on ship-change's conduct step, such as prompt = "/myteam:conduct --prompt {brief}", reading {brief}, {slice} and {handback} while the daemon's gate still checks the result) and a workflow (the team's own workflow built from the primitives). Each example is a TOML file under docs/examples/byo/ that a test keeps passing rhiza workflow check.

fields.question: Change set 01M79KHH also says 'rhiza init asks which agent the project uses'. Today init is non-interactive, there is no project agent setting, and run start / session start / skill check take --agent with the built-in default adapter. How should init ask and what does the answer do?
fields.reasoning: Asking without storing the answer would change nothing a run does; a project setting in git config matches where the other project settings (rhiza.ship.*, rhiza.autonomy.*) live and is read the same way by run start, session start and skill check, which today fall back to adapter.Default(). Taking the default silently without a terminal keeps scripted inits and the testscripts working unchanged. Listing adapter.Names() keeps the agents-named-only-in-adapters constraint.
fields.statement: rhiza init takes --agent <adapter>; with no flag and a terminal on stdin it lists the registered adapters and asks, the default preselected (an empty answer takes it); with no terminal (scripts, --json) it takes the default without asking. The answer is stored in a new project setting rhiza.project.agent (git config), which run start, session start and skill check use when --agent is unset; an explicit --agent still wins. Adapter names come from the adapter registry, so nothing outside an adapter names an agent.

fields.question: Where does the hand-written primitives reference go? (docs/reference/ holds only files `rhiza docs` generates.)
fields.reasoning: docs/reference/ holds only files rhiza docs generates and rhiza check compares; the primitives page explains how step kinds and commands combine, which is prose rather than a key table, so it sits beside custom-workflows.md and links workflow-file.md for the keys instead of duplicating them.
fields.statement: The primitives reference is a hand-written docs/primitives.md: each primitive (agent, spawn, gate, push/pr, wait, merge, signoff, hook) with the step kind or command that is it, its outcomes and how a red hands back; it links the generated workflow-file reference for the keys and is linked from the README, runs-and-daemon.md and custom-workflows.md.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestProjectAgent' covers the setting unset (the default adapter), set (run start's agent steps, session start and skill check take it), an explicit --agent overriding it, and daemon set refusing an unknown adapter name with the registered names in the message; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(project-agent|docs-reference-config|describe-golden)' passes, project-agent.txtar new, after rhiza docs regenerates docs/reference/config.md and describe-golden is -update'd if a request type changed. Touches internal/api/daemon_settings.go, internal/api/session.go, internal/api/run.go (run start's agent), internal/api/skill_check.go, docs/reference/config.md and cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/project-agent.txtar; names no agent outside internal/adapter.
fields.statement: A project setting rhiza.project.agent (git config, listed by rhiza daemon settings and in docs/reference/config.md) names the agent adapter the project uses; rhiza daemon set refuses a name the adapter registry does not know, listing the registered names; rhiza run start, rhiza session start and rhiza skill check use it when --agent is unset, an explicit --agent still wins, and unset keeps the registered default adapter.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestInit' covers --agent writing rhiza.project.agent, an unknown --agent refused with the registered names and no .rhiza created, the prompt driven through a fake terminal (default on an empty line, a re-ask on an unknown name, a chosen name stored) and no prompt when stdin is not a terminal; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(init|root-init|describe-golden)' passes, init.txtar extended for --agent, the non-terminal default and the no-git case, describe-golden -update'd. Touches internal/api/init.go, internal/api/init_test.go, cmd/rhiza (only if the terminal check must live in the CLI frame), cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/init.txtar, describe-golden.txtar and docs/reference/cli.md (rhiza docs); names no agent outside internal/adapter.
fields.statement: rhiza init asks which agent the project uses: --agent <adapter> answers it (an unknown name is a usage error listing the registered adapters, and nothing is created); with no flag, not --json, and a terminal on stdin it prints the registered adapters with the default marked and reads one line (empty takes the default, an unknown name asks again); with no terminal it takes the default without asking; inside a git repository it writes the answer to rhiza.project.agent, outside one it writes no setting and says how to set it later with rhiza daemon set; its output and --json response name the agent.

fields.acceptance: A test in cmd/rhiza (docs_primitives_test.go, new) fails unless docs/primitives.md has a section for each of the eight primitives and names every step kind workflow.Kinds (or the step-kind list rhiza docs renders) reports; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestDocsPrimitives|TestScripts/(docs-commands-exist|docs-links)' passes; make self-check passes (rhiza check finds every rhiza command the page names and every link resolves). Touches docs/primitives.md (new), README.md, docs/runs-and-daemon.md, docs/custom-workflows.md and cmd/rhiza/docs_primitives_test.go.
fields.statement: docs/primitives.md is the primitives reference in the docs' plain style: for each of agent, spawn, gate, push/pr, wait, merge, signoff and hook it says what it does, the step kind or rhiza command that is it (agent step, rhiza run spawn, gate step, rhiza ship open-pr, wait step, rhiza ship merge, signoff step, command step and [[cleanup]]), its outcomes and how a red result hands back to an agent step (handback:<step>, handback_cap); it links docs/reference/workflow-file.md for the keys, and the README, docs/runs-and-daemon.md and docs/custom-workflows.md link it.

fields.acceptance: TestDocsExampleWorkflows (cmd/rhiza/docs_examples_test.go), extended to docs/examples/byo/*.toml, fails unless all three examples (skill.toml, conductor.toml, workflow.toml) pass rhiza workflow check; a test fails unless docs/bring-your-own-agent.md includes or links each example file; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestDocsExampleWorkflows|TestDocsBringYourOwn|TestScripts/docs-commands-exist' passes; make self-check passes. Touches docs/bring-your-own-agent.md (new), docs/examples/byo/ (new), README.md, docs/agents.md, docs/custom-workflows.md and cmd/rhiza/docs_examples_test.go.
fields.statement: docs/bring-your-own-agent.md, in the docs' plain style, shows a team bringing its own agent at three levels with one worked example each: a skill (rhiza skill check on the team's invoke, then that invoke in a role table of a workflow forked from ship-change-classic), a conductor (the team's conduct skill as ship-change's conduct prompt, reading {brief}, {slice} and {handback}, with the gate's checks it must still pass) and a workflow (the team's own steps from the primitives); it covers rhiza init --agent and rhiza.project.agent, links docs/primitives.md, and is linked from the README, docs/agents.md and docs/custom-workflows.md; each example is a file under docs/examples/byo/.
